record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether independently trained networks learn the same solution using function-space agreement and mechanistic analysis, but does not test delayed generalization or the grokking training trajectory.
record.gate_note: The paper reports high rank-classification accuracy and several mechanistic findings, but does not measure training and test accuracy over optimization or test a delayed-generalization effect. It also does not test dataset-size-dependent delays, initialization or weight-norm transitions, realistic large-model training, an efficiency threshold, or optimizer/numerical artifact controls. Those results are not rows for the listed versions. The results relevant to V6 are the reported agreement and shared solution structure across independently trained models.
record.test_reason: The paper does not study grokking: there is no delayed generalization, training-curve analysis or algorithmic task. It does report results across 50 random seeds of one transformer trained on elliptic-curve rank classification: function-space agreement, prime-position attention in every model, consistent L-value encoding, and broad mechanistic structure said to be the same. These bear on V6, whether runs converge to the same algorithm, in a new non-algorithmic setting (T3 rather than T2). Only seed variation is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The main conclusion is that a transformer trained on Frobenius traces rediscovers the Mestre-Nagao heuristic via a sparse push-pull layer-1 MLP circuit, with a suboptimal readout. Attention is dissociated from causal importance, and the CLS embedding encodes log L(E,1). The 50 seed models compute effectively the same function despite large weight-space barriers. Grokking is not discussed; Nanda et al. is cited only as a method reference.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains a transformer for elliptic-curve rank classification on a large curve dataset and analyzes its learned mechanism. It does not use the small-dataset overfit-then-delayed-generalization measurement or training procedure needed to test grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight-space linear-interpolation barriers between the 50 seed models are large (mean 0.556) without permutation alignment, despite near-identical functions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained solutions are functionally equivalent but not linearly mode-connected in raw weight space.

record.problems: Only one architecture and training setup are used for the across-run comparison. Prediction agreement and qualitative shared structure do not establish exact algorithm identity, and the paper does not test dependence on architecture or hyperparameters.

untested.parts: Dependence on architecture or hyperparameters is not tested; only random seeds vary. Neuron-level circuit identity across runs is not tested; the circuit analysis covers only the centroid model. The setting is not grokking: no small algorithmic dataset and no delayed generalization.
Not tested: no training-time accuracy curves, no delay and no dataset-size sweep.
Not tested: no time course of circuit formation.
Not tested: no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation and no delayed generalization.
Not tested. Weight decay is fixed at 0.01 and there is no dataset-size threshold.

missing.what: Prime-position CLS attention across all 50 models: 198/200 layer-0 heads prefer primes; per-model mean ratios 2.1x–50x (median 6.5x).
Linear probe of the CLS embedding for log L(E,1) across 50 models: R2 0.944±0.011 (0.962±0.011 after controlling for conductor).
Direct logit attribution across 50 models: the layer-1 MLP dominates (3.2x the layer-0 MLP, 7.5x the heads).

record.verdict_notes: The V6 link is weak. The setting is not grokking, and the strongest-looking number (agreement above 98.8%) is implied by about 99% accuracy per model. The cross-run evidence for a shared mechanism is the coarse signatures in sections 5–7.2, which the rows do not capture. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No training-time accuracy trajectory, overfitting-to-generalization delay, or training-set-size sweep.
No time-course analysis of circuit formation or removal of memorizing components, and no test of whether progress measures anticipate a generalization jump.
No non-algorithmic data experiment and no initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning experiment on realistic data.
Weight decay is used in training, but its causal role, a critical dataset size, and ungrokking are not tested.
Tests agreement across random seeds for one architecture and training setup; does not vary architecture or hyperparameters, or establish exact identity of the learned algorithms.
No controlled comparison of adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax effects.
